_comment: The hand-written half of frame_parity.json: which cross-platform frame disagreements are a platform idiom (category 3), on which fields, and why. `jui conformance frame-parity --update` measures, applies these rules (the first rule whose fixture / id globs match wins; fields: the fields allowed to differ), and writes frame_parity.json. A matched id that also differs OUTSIDE its rule's fields is not ledgered and is named, so a defect cannot ride in with an idiom on the same id. A rule with no fields keeps its ids out on purpose. `expected` ({host: {field: value}}) pins the named faces to a stated amount within the gate's tolerance, the unnamed faces must agree, or the id is refused. HAND-MAINTAINED.

rules.reason: iOS draws no multiple on the first line (SwiftUI has no per-line height; 2026-10-05 user instruction, attribute_semantics lineHeightMultipleBase): five lines of L 20.33 at m 1.8 are L + 4 x m x L = 166.71, (m - 1) x L = 16.27 short of 5 x m x L. Android draws each line on the pixel grid (KotlinJsonUI LabelLineHeight: 43.2 dp is 86.4 px, drawn 86 at density 2 on conf_ci and the CI pixel_tablet), 0.2 short a line: 215.0 for five. Web draws the declared 5 x m x L = 216.0. All three are pinned (naming two would leave the third compared with nothing): any other height on any face is refused
NOT LEDGERED: triage — android is exactly 800; check for a cap before pinning
